workflowStatuses.description: Being prepared and not yet ready for use. Typically used for new master-data records, transactions, or maintenance orders while details are captured before submission or activation.
Removed from normal grids after completing its lifecycle. Typically used for records that have been deliberately retired from normal operations while retained references support historical integrity.
Retained for historical reference and hidden from normal grids. Typically used for inactive master data or completed records that are no longer needed in day-to-day processing.
Active and available for use. Typically used for operational master data such as customers, suppliers, properties, or contracts after the required setup or approval.
Temporarily prevented from use. Typically used for customer, supplier, or other master-data records placed on hold pending investigation, compliance checks, or corrective action.

Submitted for the next review or processing action. Typically used for master-data approval requests, transactions awaiting posting, maintenance orders awaiting allocation, or insurance claims awaiting assessment.
Awaiting approval to archive. Typically used when a user requests retirement of a master-data record and an authorised reviewer must approve the request.
Awaiting approval to return to active use. Typically used when an archived or blocked master-data record is requested for renewed operational use.
Awaiting assignment of the team responsible for the work. Typically used for maintenance orders after submission and before a crew or responsible resources are allocated.
Work or engagement is underway. Typically used for maintenance orders being carried out or sales leads being contacted and qualified.
The reported issue has been resolved. Typically used for maintenance orders after the repair or service is completed, before final review and closure.
Cancelled before completion. Typically used for maintenance orders or other work requests that are no longer required or will not proceed.

The process has been closed. Typically used for completed maintenance orders, concluded insurance claims, or sales leads requiring no further follow-up. Availability remains subject to the workflow setting.

Posted to the accounting records. Typically used for journals or other accounting transactions after successful posting validation; it distinguishes recorded accounting entries from drafts or submissions.
Reported and awaiting assessment. Typically used for an insurance claim after the loss or incident is recorded and before assessment begins.
Under assessment before a decision is made. Typically used for insurance claims while evidence, coverage, liability, and the potential settlement are evaluated.
Approved for subsequent processing. Typically used for insurance claims accepted for settlement or other records that have passed an authorised review.
Settlement has started with an outstanding balance remaining. Typically used for insurance claims where only part of the agreed settlement has been paid or otherwise fulfilled.
Settlement has been completed. Typically used for insurance claims after the agreed settlement is fulfilled and before administrative closure.
Reviewed and declined. Typically used for insurance claims where assessment concludes that the claim will not be accepted for settlement.
Withdrawn from further processing. Typically used for insurance claims or requests that the submitting party chooses not to pursue.
Newly recorded and awaiting initial processing. Typically used for sales leads before contact, qualification, or assignment of follow-up activity.

Marked as having progressed to the next business process or record. Typically used for sales leads that have become opportunities or customers; this status alone does not create the resulting records.
Open for opportunity activity and allocation. Typically used for sales opportunities being qualified or developed before proposal, negotiation, or a final outcome.
A proposal is being prepared or considered. Typically used for sales opportunities while a quotation, proposed scope, or commercial offer is developed and reviewed with the prospect.
Commercial terms are under negotiation. Typically used for sales opportunities while pricing, scope, or contract terms are being agreed before the opportunity is won or lost.

Opportunity won; further cost and revenue allocations are disabled in the seeded workflow. Typically used when the prospect accepts the offer and the opportunity process concludes; subsequent delivery can be managed through an appropriate project or other accounting object.

Opportunity lost; further cost and revenue allocations are disabled in the seeded workflow. Typically used when the prospect rejects the offer, selects another supplier, or otherwise ends the opportunity without a sale.
